title: Building Projects with AI
subtitle: From clear requests to judgment, verification and delivery
audience: People who have tried AI coding but lack an overview of project development. No prior Python, Git or terminal experience is required.
baseline: Tool-neutral, using a personal study-list webpage throughout. Practice decisions in the book, then work in a separate directory. Commands use Git 2.28+ and Node.js 22.12+ capabilities; QA.md records the actual verification environment.
outcomes: Turn an idea into a user scenario, first-release scope and acceptance cases
Explain the roles of files, data, browsers and servers
Make focused Git commits and distinguish local commits, pushes, PRs and deployment
Give an agent accurate context and tasks, then inspect important changes
Use reproduction, boundary cases and requirements to judge results
Deliver a runnable small project with backups, recovery and clear limitations
outOfScope: Full algorithms and language training for professional engineering
Implementation of realtime collaboration, payments, authentication or production databases
Cloud account registration, paid service selection and automatic deployment
Advanced Git history rewriting, complex rebases and merge-commit reverts
Guaranteed prompt outcomes, arbitrary code execution or runtime model services

chapters.title: Define the problem
chapters.objective: Describe one real scenario, narrow the first release and agree on observable completion criteria.

chapters.title: Understand how a project runs
chapters.objective: Locate entry points, trace data and follow instructions to run locally.

chapters.title: Keep recoverable records with Git
chapters.objective: Distinguish working tree, index and commits; understand branches, remotes, PRs and recovery.

chapters.title: Work with an agent
chapters.objective: Provide accurate context, give small tasks, review changes and require verification evidence.

chapters.title: Judge reliability
chapters.objective: Choose tests yourself, reproduce failures and maintain data and permission boundaries.

chapters.title: Finish and deliver a small project
chapters.objective: Choose suitable storage, check the published version and deliver something runnable and explainable.
